question:
Patient note:
A 97-year-old man who has lived independently in a one-level bungalow and still conducts his own grocery shopping was found early this morning by his visiting niece sitting at the kitchen table complaining of a “heavy chest” after a night of intermittent cough productive of thin, yellow-tinged sputum; she reported that he manages chronic osteoarthritis with over-the-counter acetaminophen only, has never been prescribed corticosteroids, biologic agents, or chemotherapy, and has no history of organ transplantation, cirrhosis, advanced pulmonary disease, or dialysis-requiring kidney injury. Emergency medical technicians arrived within twelve minutes, noted the patient to be upright, conversant, and oriented, with fingertip saturation readings fluctuating between 86 % and 88 % on ambient air; they applied a Venturi collar delivering precisely 30 % inspired oxygen verified by an inline analyzer and placed a single 20-gauge peripheral intravenous catheter that remained saline-locked. During the ten-minute transport he received no intravenous fluids, bronchodilators, antibiotics, vasopressors, diuretics, analgesics, or antipyretics. On wheel-in to the medical intensive-care receiving bay—and before any hospital interventions or change in oxygen delivery—first set of vital signs captured on two independent monitors showed an oral temperature of 98.8 °F, a regular pulse of 86 beats per minute, a respiratory rate counted over a full minute at 17 breaths per minute without accessory muscle recruitment, and a non-invasive blood pressure reproducibly cycling at 135⁄76 mm Hg on both arms. The patient opened his eyes spontaneously, answered every orientation question correctly, recalled breakfast contents, and followed complex three-step commands, establishing a Glasgow Coma Score of 15 in the absence of sedatives, alcohol, or head trauma. Skin examination revealed warm, pink extremities with capillary refill under two seconds, no peripheral edema, and no rash or petechiae. Neck veins were flat at 30°, carotid upstrokes were brisk, and radial plus dorsalis pedis pulses were 2+ bilaterally. Cardiac auscultation disclosed a crisp S1, physiologic splitting of S2, and no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Breath sounds were diffusely diminished at the right base with scattered late-inspiratory crackles; percussion there was mildly dull and tactile fremitus was increased, while the left lung field was clear. The abdomen was flat, moved with respiration, and was nontender with active bowel sounds; there was no costovertebral angle tenderness. Extremities exhibited full range of motion with symmetric strength, and a brief cerebellar screen was unremarkable. Seven minutes after bay placement—while the same 30 % Venturi source remained untouched—a right radial arterial specimen was analyzed, revealing a pH of 7.40, PaCO₂ 38 mm Hg, and a PaO₂ of 58 mm Hg, confirming moderate hypoxemia despite supplemental oxygen; end-tidal capnography displayed 37 mm Hg, corroborating the arterial CO₂. Simultaneous point-of-care metabolic panel reported sodium 141 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, chloride 103 mmol/L, bicarbonate 23 mmol/L, glucose 112 mg/dL, blood urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL, and creatinine 1.3 mg/dL—values comparable to outpatient labs drawn at his annual wellness visit three months prior, indicating preserved renal function without acute insult. A complete blood count returned a white-cell concentration of 11 300 cells/mm³ with 78 % segmented neutrophils, hematocrit 39 %, hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, and platelets 224 000/µL. Venous lactate measured 1.6 mmol/L. Portable anteroposterior chest radiography performed before any antimicrobial, steroid, or diuretic therapy depicted a right lower-lobe infiltrate with subtle air bronchograms, clear costophrenic angles, and a normal cardiac silhouette. Point-of-care lung ultrasound corroborated focal consolidation in the posterior right base with dynamic air bronchograms and preserved lung sliding elsewhere. Focused transthoracic echocardiography revealed a small, vigorously contracting left ventricle with no regional wall-motion abnormalities and an inferior vena cava diameter of 1.5 cm that collapsed more than 50 % with inspiration, suggesting adequate preload and no overt right-heart strain. Twelve-lead electrocardiography printed during the arterial draw showed normal sinus rhythm at 88 beats per minute, PR interval 160 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 420 ms, and no ischemic ST-T changes. A bladder scan registered 120 mL, and the patient reported voiding normally overnight. Importantly, from the moment the niece dialed emergency services through handoff to the intensive-care fellow—a span of roughly thirty minutes—he had not received crystalloid boluses, inhaled bronchodilators, systemic antibiotics, corticosteroids, vasopressors, narcotic analgesics, or antipyretics; the sole intervention remained the Venturi collar delivering 30 % oxygen. Consequently, the contemporaneous measurements—temperature 98.8 °F, systolic pressure 135 mm Hg, diastolic pressure 76 mm Hg, heart rate 86 beats per minute, respiratory rate 17 per minute, arterial pH 7.40, serum sodium 141 mmol/L, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, hematocrit 39 %, white blood cell count 11 300 /mm³, fraction of inspired oxygen 30 %, and arterial oxygen tension 58 mm Hg—represent an untreated physiologic snapshot at presentation for suspected community-acquired pneumonia complicated by early hypoxemic respiratory compromise in a very elderly yet cognitively intact and immunocompetent individual with preserved baseline organ function.

Question: What is the patient's APACHE II score?
solution:
APACHE II adds acute physiology, age, and chronic health points. It ordinarily uses the worst values in the first 24 hours; here the available values are from admission.
- Temperature 98.8 °F (37.1 °C): 0. Mean arterial pressure = (135 + 2 × 76)/3 ≈ 96 mm Hg: 0. Heart rate 86/min: 0. Respiratory rate 17/min: 0.
- Oxygenation: FiO₂ 0.30 is below 0.50, so use PaO₂ rather than the alveolar–arterial gradient. PaO₂ 58 mm Hg falls in the 55–60 band: 3 points.
- Arterial pH 7.40: 0. Sodium 141: 0. Potassium 4.1: 0. Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL: 0.
- Hematocrit 39%: 0. WBC 11.3 × 10⁹/L: 0. Neurologic points = 15 − GCS 15 = 0.
- Age 97 (≥75): 6. No qualifying severe chronic organ insufficiency or immunosuppression: 0.
Total = 3 acute physiology + 6 age + 0 chronic health = 9.
Final answer: 9
